failure.summary: Hair R05-M3 proves pinned roots, three-mode guide response, bounded motion and release damping, but does not bind rest/deformed guide centerlines or measure local segment stretch and total arc-length drift. A positional target can therefore be met without evidence that the guide bent rather than lengthened.

gate: Preserve R05-M3 root-pin, reduced-bending, release, static-image and freshness evidence; this Candidate does not reopen those claims.
Bind exact rest and deformed 81-node guide centerlines and calculate both per-segment strain and total arc-length drift for midshaft grab, endpoint grab, wind and release frames.
A total-length-only metric is insufficient because adjacent segments can stretch and compress while total length cancels out.
Thresholds must be scoped to the exact Hair task and justified by the intended claim or accepted baseline; classifier fixture numbers are not production thresholds.
Before a scoped pass, inject a known stretched guide and prove the independent verifier rejects it.

A pass proves only bounded centerline inextensibility for the tested guide/motion envelope. It does not prove twist, collision, self-contact, body/clothing contact, full rod physics, performance or USER-ACCEPTED.

teacherCandidate.name: Muller-Kim-Chentanez dynamic Follow-The-Leader / PositionBasedDynamics distance constraints
teacherCandidate.boundedNovelty: Defines inextensibility as adjacent rest-distance preservation and supplies a geometric single-pass hair method, while R05-M3 currently measures displacement and modal energy but no segment-length invariant.
teacherCandidate.maintenance: Repository head 10a70bc146a97873dc3c8fef372f5217e010542e dated 2026-09-01; latest tagged release 2.2.0 dated 2022-12-13, so current source activity exists but release cadence is stale.
teacherCandidate.runnableEvidence: CMake C++ library, Python interface, demos including Cosserat rods, and Linux/Windows build workflows; no dedicated Tests directory found at the audited head.
teacherCandidate.license: MIT for repository code; paper is used as source evidence only.
teacherCandidate.dependencyRisk: Direct integration requires C++/CMake/Eigen and would change the solver architecture. This Candidate imports no code or assets.
teacherCandidate.methodBoundary: Dynamic FTL trades accuracy for speed and introduces artificial damping; PBD is visually plausible but generally less accurate than force-based methods. Neither source alone validates R05 twist, contact or user quality.
teacherCandidate.auditionUse: Learn only the segment-distance invariant, positive-control design and explicit damping boundary. Solver adoption remains NOT_PROPOSED.

externalEvidence.source: Muller, Kim, Chentanez — Fast Simulation of Inextensible Hair and Fur (2012)
externalEvidence.use: Treats hair inextensibility as adjacent particle distance preservation, guarantees zero stretch with single-pass Follow-The-Leader, and discloses artificial damping/accuracy tradeoffs.

Runnable MIT implementation exposes distance-constraint projection against a declared rest length plus rod demos and build workflows; used only as an implementation teacher for the invariant, not imported.
